paper_summary: This paper presents Sun-as-a-star analyses of spatially integrated Hα spectra to investigate various solar active events, such as flares, filament eruptions, and off-limb prominence eruptions. The primary dataset is from the Solar Dynamics Doppler Imager (SDDI) on SMART at Hida Observatory, with complementary data from GOES soft X-ray measurements, SOHO/LASCO coronagraph images, and SDO/AIA multi-wavelength imagery. These instruments are used to identify event timing, verify CME occurrence, and interpret event scenarios for events between November 2016 and May 2021.

instruments.name: SMART/SDDI (Solar Dynamics Doppler Imager on the Solar Magnetic Activity Research Telescope)
instruments.general_comments: The backbone of the study, SDDI captures full-disk solar images in Hα at 73 wavelengths, enabling Sun-as-a-star analyses by integrating spectra over selected regions. It has operated routinely since May 2016, covering all analyzed events.
general_quotes: The Solar Dynamics Doppler Imager (SDDI; Ichimoto et al. 2017) is installed on the Solar Magnetic Activity Research Telescope (SMART; Ueno et al. 2004) at Hida Observatory, Kyoto University. It takes full-disk solar images at 73 wavelengths from the Hα line center −9.0 ˚A to the Hα line center +9.0 ˚A with a time cadence of 12−16 sec... The SDDI has been observing the Sun routinely since 2016 May and has stored the Hα spectral images of various active events.

data_collection_periods.physical_observable: Hα spectral profiles showing emission, absorption, red/blue shifts, and line broadening linked to flares, filament eruptions, and prominence motions.
physobs_quotes: Sun-as-a-star Hα spectra exhibit different features depending on the causes of the emission: (i) Flares show emission at the Hα line center with red asymmetry and line broadening; (ii) Filament eruptions show blue-/red-shifted absorptions; (iii) Eruptions of offlimb prominences show shifted emissions.
